summary.text: Rain streams down a night bus window while blurred city lights slide past outside.

description.text: At night, rain gathers on the outside of a bus window in a dense scatter of beads, each droplet catching thin amber and white reflections from the city beyond. The glass fills the view in close, intimate detail: water clings in trembling domes, then breaks into wavering trails that run downward and bunch along the lower edge of the pane. Behind the wet surface, the city is reduced to soft blocks of light, red tail lamps, pale shop signs, and dark building shapes that slide slowly past. Reflections of those lights travel across the glass and stretch into long, liquid streaks, mingling with the rain so that the window seems to hold two moving layers at once. A few larger drops land near the center, shudder, and join the current, drawing fresh channels through the condensation. The passing lights shift from warm amber to cool white and back again, their blurred edges trembling whenever the bus changes speed. Along the frame, the dark interior stays almost invisible, leaving only a faint suggestion of the window edge and the night pressing close beyond it. The rain sound remains steady against the pane, accompanied by a low, muffled engine hum and the soft wash of tires over wet asphalt. Over the five seconds, the trails lengthen, the reflections drag farther across the glass, and the city outside continues its slow slide, preserving a quiet, observational mood without any added music or voices.
Rain beads cling to the bus window while blurred city lights and dark building shapes sit beyond the wet glass.
Rain ticks softly against the glass over a low, muffled bus hum.
Small droplets tremble, merge, and begin to run downward in wavering trails.
